In the right-hand thumb rule, the thumb is directed towards the direction of the current (or motion of a positively charged particle).

This rule is commonly used in electromagnetism to determine the direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor or the force on a moving charge in a magnetic field.

This rule is a fundamental tool in physics for visualizing and solving problems related to electromagnetism.

How it works:

- If you point your thumb in the direction of the current (or motion of a positive charge), the curled fingers will indicate the direction of the magnetic field lines around the conductor.

- Conversely, if you point your fingers in the direction of the magnetic field and your thumb in the direction of the current, your palm will face the direction of the force acting on the conductor.

Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) is a scheme launched by the Hon'ble Prime Minister on April 8, 2015, for providing loans up to Rs 10 lakh to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro-enterprises.

These loans are classified as MUDRA loans under PMMY. These loans are given by Commercial Banks, RRBs, Small Finance Banks, Cooperative Banks, MFIs, and NBFCs.

Under the aegis of PMMY, MUDRA has created three products namely Shishu, Kishore, and Tarun to signify the stage of growth/development and funding needs of the beneficiary micro unit/entrepreneur and also provide a reference point for the next phase of graduation/growth.

The Mavilan tribe inhabits Kasaragod and Kannur districts of Kerala and have been practising this dance form as an important part of their tradition.

Article 35 lays down that the power to make laws, to give effect to certain specified fundamental rights shall vest only in the Parliament and not in the state legislatures. This provision ensures that there is uniformity throughout

India with regard to the nature of those fundamental rights and punishment for their infringement. In this direction, Article 35 contains the following provisions:

The Parliament shall have (and the legislature of a state shall not have) power to make laws with respect to the following matters:

Prescribing residence as a condition for certain employment or appointments in a state or union territory or local authority or other authority (Article 16).

Empowering courts other than the Supreme Court and the high courts to issue directions, orders and writs of all kinds for the enforcement of fundamental rights (Article 32).

Restricting or abrogating the application of Fundamental Rights to members of armed forces, police forces, etc. (Article 33).

Indemnifying any government servant or any other person for any act done during the operation of martial law in any area (Article 34).

The Rowlatt Act, referred to as the "black act" was passed by the British government in 1919, during the First World War. It was named after the Rowlatt Committee's president Sir Sidney Rowlatt.

The aim of enforcing this act was to abolish revolt and uproot conspiracy against the British from India. The Rowlatt Act entitled the British to arrest anyone found suspicious of plotting against the British Raj.

Under this act, those supposed to be involved in revolt against the British could be sentenced to a term of up to 2 years in jail, without any trial. Any suspects could be arrested without warrant and could be detained for indefinite period.

The act also empowered the government to silence the press in case they wanted to investigate the reasons and the evidences. Resultantly, there was a ban on public gatherings of any cultural or religious sort. Thus, this law was strongly opposed by the Indians.

Mahatma Gandhi among the many was also against this law and organized a "hartal," a form of protest through non-violence by stoppage of work and going on hunger strike. This "hartal" was organized on 6th April.

questions.solution:
In such cases where the sentence takes an Interrogative form in Direct Speech, "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", and "asked", etc. in Indirect Speech are changed into "said" in Direct Speech.

In Direct speech, the verb is always placed before the subject, unlike in Indirect Speech.

If there is a question whose answer can come as "Yes" or "No", we remove the inverted commas and add the conjunction "If" or "Whether" in the Indirect Speech and the verb/s "Is/are/am/was/were" before the subject, in Direct Speech.

For example:

Ravi asked me if she was studying. (Indirect Speech)

Ravi said to me, "Is she studying?" (Direct Speech)

The tense of the Indirect Speech is in the past perfect tense. So, the tense in the Direct Speech will be in the present perfect tense.

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

"asked them whether" changes to "said to them".

"had" changes to "have".

"They" changes to "you".

Therefore, the correct answer is: "I said to them, "Have you completed the task?""

Hence, option (a) is correct.

In the context of the sentence, "elucidating molecular mechanisms" suggests that recent advancements in biotechnology research are aimed at clarifying and understanding the intricate details of molecular mechanisms involved in agricultural processes.

"Muddling" means to confuse.

No other word can fit in the blank contextually.

Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank. The pilot told the cabin crew to _____ for take-off.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

The pilot told the cabin crew to _____ for take-off.
questions.solution:
The most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank is "stand by." "Stand by" means to be ready or prepared to take action. In the context of the given sentence, it indicates that the pilot instructed the cabin crew to be prepared for take-off. Other phrasal verbs do not fit the context of the sentence. "Bear away" means to steer a ship away from something, "turn down" means to refuse an offer or request, and "look down on" means to view someone or something as inferior. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

The complete sentence is: The pilot told the cabin crew to stand by for take-off.

NOTE:

Phrasal verb: A phrase that consists of a verb with a preposition or adverb or both, the meaning of which is different from the meaning of its separate parts. Example: She has always looked down on me. Here, the phrasal verb 'to look down on someone' doesn't mean that you are looking down from a higher place at someone who is below you; it means that you think that you are better than someone.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Sarah tends to _____ when she's running late for appointments.

"Break the bank" means spending so much money that it causes financial difficulty. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

The complete sentence is: Sarah tends to get in a sweat when she's running late for appointments.

questions.question: Select the sentence that is expressed in passive voice.
questions.questionHtml: Select the sentence that is expressed in passive voice.

options.text: Rimi moved the sofa to the hall.

options.text: Cold showers normally represent summer seasons.
options.html: Cold showers normally represent summer seasons.

options.text: She transferred us all her pending debt amount.
options.html: She transferred us all her pending debt amount.

questions.solution:
The structure of a passive voice is Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + V3 [+ by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case)].

The passive voice is used when the subject of a sentence is acted upon by the verb. In option c), the subject 'the road' is being acted upon by the verb 'blocked'. This makes it the passive voice. The other sentences are in the active voice because the subject is performing the action.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent sentence. A. Sponsors' money B. The study implies C. Reduces risk and saves D. A considerable amount of E. That appropriate asset and liability management
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent sentence.

A. Sponsors' money

B. The study implies

C. Reduces risk and saves

D. A considerable amount of

E. That appropriate asset and liability management
questions.solution:
The correct order to form a meaningful and coherent sentence is BECDA. Part B indicates that a study implies something. Part E comes next as it specifies what the study implies or suggests should be done - appropriate asset and liability management. Part C then explains the benefit or outcome of appropriate asset and liability management (reduction of risk and saving of something). Accordingly, EC forms a logical pair. Parts D and A then specify what is saved (a considerable amount of sponsor's money). Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

The complete sentence is: The study implies that appropriate asset and liability management reduces risk and saves a considerable amount of sponsors' money.

questions.question: Select the sentence in which the '-ing' form of verb expresses the continuity of an action/event.
questions.questionHtml: Select the sentence in which the '-ing' form of verb expresses the continuity of an action/event.

options.text: Jogging is a great way to stay healthy.
options.html: Jogging is a great way to stay healthy.

options.text: She enjoys listening to classical music.
options.html: She enjoys listening to classical music.

options.text: I cannot talk right now; I am working on an important project.
options.html: I cannot talk right now; I am working on an important project.

options.text: He suggested going for a walk in the park.
options.html: He suggested going for a walk in the park.

questions.solution:
Among the given options, (c) is the best fit because the "-ing" form of the verb "working" is used to express the continuity of an action/event in the present moment. The construction "am working" indicates that the action is ongoing. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

(a)- uses the gerund "Jogging," which functions as a noun in this sentence, not to express continuity.

(b)- uses the gerund "listening" to indicate an activity she enjoys, but it does not express the continuity of the action.

(d)- uses the gerund "going," which indicates the action as a noun (suggesting the idea of a walk), not an ongoing event.

Note: Gerund: Gerund is a verb form that functions as a noun, ending in -ing. A gerund can be either the subject or object of a sentence in English. Example: "Everybody enjoyed her dancing and singing at the party." The words 'dancing' and 'singing' are gerunds.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If you need a ride to the airport, I will done the honours of driving you there.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

If you need a ride to the airport, I will done the honours of driving you there.
questions.solution:
The segment that contains a grammatical error is 'I will done the honours'. The error is related to the verb "done." When we form future tense sentences with "will," we use the base form of the verb that follows "will." The correct form in this case should be "do", not "done" [past tense verb]. "Do" is the base form of the verb that should follow "will" to indicate the action of driving. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: If you need a ride to the airport, I will do the honours of driving you there.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. My parents forbid to me from staying out past midnight on weekdays.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

My parents forbid to me from staying out past midnight on weekdays.
questions.solution:
'To' should not be used with the following verbs when followed by an object. Such verbs are- advise, welcome, ask, warm, forbid, order, remind, compliment, etc. So, drop 'to' from 'forbid to me'.

The correct sentence is - My parents forbid me from staying out past midnight on weekdays.

Hence, option (a) is correct.

questions.solution: The phrase highlighted in the given sentence is incorrect and needs replacement with the correct one. When determiners 'many', 'more' and 'most' are used, nouns or pronouns following these should be plural; thus 'customer' is incorrect, and options a) and d) are eliminated. The adverb 'likely' is qualifying the verb 'are trending' stated in the first clause of the sentence; this makes option (c) the correct answer.
